title: Seller sprint pocket playset — unplugged
audience: Field sellers and SEs — 5-minute rapid prep before demo or pilot kickoff
summary: Micro-deck to give sellers a compact, conversation-first playset for rapid pilot qualification and escalation. Focus: 1) tight value hooks, 2) technical guardrails and fallback patterns, 3) minimal pilot plan that reduces operational risk and accelerates conversion.
content:
Slide 1 — One-liner hook and purpose:
- Hook: "Make inference predictable — fast, cheap, and recoverable"
- Tell them in one line: Redwood gives predictable latency and clear cost levers so your customer can ship LLM features without infrastructure surprise.
Speaker note: start with customer problem (unpredictable tail latency / surprise GPU bills). Use a micro-case: "search summarization went from 1.1s median to 3s tail during peak."

Slide 2 — 3 quick value points (30s):
- Production-first: throughput & latency SLOs, autoscaling with reserved capacity fallback.
- Cost controls: batching/caching + quantization recommendations tuned to workload.
- Operational escape hatches: model variants, regional fallback, and automatic sacrifice-to-cost policies.
Speaker note: name a concrete #s if you have them for the account (e.g., expected tokens / month).

Slide 3 — Pilot light plan (buyer friendly, 2-week cadence):
1) Week 0: small ingestion + synthetic traffic to validate latency profile (1–2 dev days).
2) Week 1: integration with a feature flag, run 1% traffic under Redwood Hosted / Dedicated faucet.
3) Week 2: expand to 10–20% with canary routing and cost telemetry dashboard.
Go/no-go criteria: tail latency < target, regression rate < X%, cost/unit within threshold.
Speaker note: emphasize tiny scope and clear success metrics — removes procurement fear.

Slide 4 — Common objections + tight responses (for SEs):
- "We can host ourselves cheaper": "Compare unit economics rather than sticker price; we surface batching/caching recommendations and show you the delta on 10k QPS profiles."
- "Latency spikes during peak": "We offer reserved capacity and fast regional fallback plus KV prefix caching to shave tail latency off."
- "Data security / compliance": "Private deployment or VPC option + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs — we’ll map the gap in the first week."
Speaker note: link to a concise architecture diagram in the follow-up email.

Slide 5 — Fallback economics cheat (quick script for seller):
- If primary model costs X per 1k tokens, fallback model costs ~0.35X with slightly lower quality.
- Use local short-term caching (prefix-based) to reduce repeated prompt cost by up to 60% for query-heavy interfaces.
- Pricing pitch: show committed dedicated pool vs bursty hosted vs hybrid — emphasize predictability.
Example script: "If your median session prints 400 tokens, switching to a compact quantized variant with prefix cache drops cost per session from $0.023 to $0.009 while keeping top-1 accuracy in 92% of cases."

Slide 6 — SE checklist for pilot kickoff (copyable into Slack/email):
- Confirm sample traffic: 5–10k queries/day representative set.
- Decide test routes + toggles (1% then 10%).
- Share latency & cost targets (numeric).
- Grant API key + CORS/IP allowlist or provide VPC details.
- Setup alerting: tail latency > threshold, cost burn rate > forecast.
Speaker note: paste this during kickoff — reduces back-and-forth.

Slide 7 — Quick fallback play examples (technical sketch):
- 1) Fallback to cheaper quantized model if cost burn > daily budget (automated policy).
- 2) Regional reroute: if region A latency > 2x baseline, route to region B with slightly higher cost but lower latency.
- 3) Graceful degrade to cached or template answer when token budget critical.
Speaker note: call out that all three are configurable and observable in the Console.

Slide 8 — Battle-ready one-liners for different buyer personas:
- CTO: "We reduce operational surprises by making the economic levers explicit and automatable."
- Platform Lead: "Same API across hosted, dedicated and private—so you don’t rewrite your stack."
- Product Manager: "Pilot in two weeks, measurable UX regressions first — lowest-risk way to ship."

Slide 9 — Closing / next steps (30s):
- Ask: "Do you have a dataset we can replay for a smoke test?"
- Offer: schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff with solutions engineering (we bring a checklist and runbook).
- Attachments to follow: minimal architecture diagram, pilot SOW template, short ROI calc sheet.

Appendix (notes for the SE):
- Quick ROI calc: show tokens/session * sessions/day * price/token for 3 model variants. Keep the sheet simple with 3 knobs (tokens/session, sessions/day, model price).
- Demo cue: show 20s live stream with and without prefix cache — highlight response consistency.
- Risks to call out: non-representative synthetic load, client-side batching hiding server savings, policy/regulatory lead times for Private deployments.

Email snippet to attach after meeting:
Subject: Next steps + pilot checklist
Body: "Thanks — here’s the pilot plan we agreed. I’ve attached the SOW template and a 30-min slot for kickoff. If you can share 5k representative queries or a small dataset we’ll smoke-test latency and cost estimates within 48 hours."

Speaker tips (voice & style):
- Keep it consultative: ask their current cost pain, not ours.
- Use concrete numbers early if they are available.
- If they push for self-hosting, offer a 2-week proof-of-concept with clear exit criteria.

End of deck.

Design notes for slides: use high contrast, one main metric per slide, callouts for "must-ask" questions, and a single CTA on closing slide.

Collateral to attach in follow-up (links referenced in linked_artifacts):
- Minimal SOW template (public doc)
- ROI calculator spreadsheet (sheet id: CON_GTM_ROI_03)
- Short architecture diagram (png id: ARCH-SMOKE-01)

Internal TODOs before publishing deck:
- PM review of pilot success criteria (Priya)
- SE runthrough with sample dataset (Marcus)
- Legal check on pilot SOW phrasing for enterprise customers (Tomás)

Unresolved questions / optional experiments:
- Add an A/B script for human-in-the-loop fallback? (low lift)
- Quick embed example that demonstrates prefix-cache effect in 30s (engineering quick win)

Footnote: this is intentionally minimal and meant to be copy/paste-friendly for fast, late-stage customer conversations.
